title: SSRF via Fragrantica Edge Function URL Parameter
description: The Supabase Edge Function scrape-fragrantica accepts a `url` parameter from the client and passes it to `fetch()` after only checking `url.includes('fragrantica.com')`. This check is bypassable: an attacker can craft URLs like `https://fragrantica.com.evil.com/`, `https://fragrantica.com@attacker.com/`, or use URL parsing tricks to reach internal services. The function also accepts a `query` parameter that is interpolated into a search URL without domain restriction.
impact: An attacker can use the edge function as a proxy to scan internal Supabase infrastructure, access internal APIs, or exfiltrate data from internal services. The Deno runtime may have access to environment variables or internal network resources.
mitigation: Implement a strict URL allowlist. Parse the URL and validate the hostname against a whitelist (only `www.fragrantica.com.br` and `www.fragrantica.com`). Use `new URL()` to parse and validate. Block all internal/private IP ranges. Add rate limiting.
critic_reasoning: The edge function is deployed and publicly accessible. The URL validation is a simple string.includes() which is well-known to be bypassable. The function makes server-side requests with the Deno runtime's network access. This is a live SSRF vector.
outrage_commentary: SSRF in a serverless function with weak URL validation is a serious issue. The function runs in the Supabase infrastructure with potential access to internal services.
executive_summary: The Fragrantica edge function accepts user-supplied URLs with weak validation (string.includes). An attacker can bypass the check to probe internal infrastructure or use the function as an open proxy.

history.details: Edge function URL validation is weak — string.includes() bypassable via URL tricks
